observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: ECX is copied to ESI at 0x00b3d637 (8b f1) and every field access is made through ESI, so the receiver arrives in ECX. No instruction reads [ESP + 0x4] before the frame is reserved, so there is no stack argument. All three exits are bare RET (0x00b3d657, 0x00b3d683, 0x00b3d695), so the callee pops nothing and the caller owns cleanup. The reconstruction is declared __attribute__((thiscall)) so clang++ -m32 -O2 reproduces the register form and the same field displacements.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: IEEE-754 single delivered on the x87 stack in ST(0). The body uses FLD and FMUL and never executes FSTP, so the value is left on the x87 register stack for the caller.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00b3d64f FLD float ptr [ESP + 0x8] and 0x00b3d678 FLD float ptr [ESP + 0x4] are the only two value producers; 0x00b3d67c and 0x00b3d68e FMUL float ptr [ESI + 0x10] are the only arithmetic. Callers confirm: 0x00b3e40c and 0x00b3e417 FSTP the result into stack locals, and 0x00b42687 FLD ST0 / 0x00b42689 FLD ST1 duplicate it, which only makes sense for a value already on the x87 stack.
observed_original_abi.frame: SUB ESP,0x8 then PUSH ESI, mirrored by POP ESI then ADD ESP,0x8
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX, moved to ESI at 0x00b3d637 and never rewritten

observed_mechanics: 0x00b3d633: XORPS XMM0,XMM0 materialises +0.0f, which is both the comparison constant and the default scale value.
0x00b3d637: MOV ESI,ECX captures the receiver; ESI is the only base register used for field access.
0x00b3d639: MOVSS XMM1,[ESI + 0x18] loads the cached override into XMM1.
0x00b3d63e: COMISS XMM1,XMM0 compares the override against +0.0f.
0x00b3d64d: JBE 0x00b3d658 is CF|ZF, so the slow path is taken when override <= 0.0f OR when the comparison is unordered; the early return therefore requires an ordered override > 0.0f.
0x00b3d64f: FLD float ptr [ESP + 0x8] returns the override verbatim, unmultiplied, bypassing the +0x10 factor entirely.
0x00b3d641: MOVSS [ESP + 0x4],XMM0 spills 0.0f as the pre-switch default; neither the 0/1 arm nor the default arm overwrites it.

0x00b3d65b SUB EAX,0x0 / 0x00b3d65e JZ, 0x00b3d660 SUB EAX,0x1 / 0x00b3d663 JZ, 0x00b3d665 SUB EAX,0x1 / 0x00b3d668 JNZ is the classic MSVC switch lowering and proves the three distinguished selector values are 0, 1 and 2.

0x00b3d684..0x00b3d68c: receiver+0x40 supplies ECX, [ECX] supplies the vtable, [vtable + 0x70] is the callee and CALL EAX dispatches it thiscall; its result arrives in ST(0) and is consumed by the FMUL, never stored.
0x00b3d66a MOV EAX,[ESI + 0x40] plus 0x00b3d66d MOVSS XMM0,[EAX + 0x44] is the selector-2 arm: it reads the float at byte offset +0x44 of the sub-object, not a virtual call.
0x00b3d67c and 0x00b3d68e: FMUL float ptr [ESI + 0x10] applies the same multiplier on both slow-path arms.
The three exits (0x00b3d657, 0x00b3d683, 0x00b3d695) are all bare RET, so stack cleanup belongs to the caller.
The body contains no CALL other than the single indirect CALL EAX, no global access, and no memory write outside its own frame.

semantic_contract: Compute this object's effective scale as a float. If the cached override field at receiver+0x18 is greater than +0.0f in an ordered comparison, return that value verbatim and do nothing else. Otherwise multiply the per-object factor at receiver+0x10 by a source magnitude chosen by the small enum at receiver+0x04: selector values 0 and 1 both call the polymorphic sub-object at receiver+0x40 through its vtable slot +0x70 and use the float it returns; selector value 2 instead reads the float at byte offset +0x44 of that sub-object; every other selector value leaves the magnitude at +0.0f, so the product is +0.0f. The receiver is never null-checked, neither is the sub-object pointer, and the function writes no field and no global. The result is returned on the x87 stack.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC: the complete body, ABI, every field offset, every constant, the switch lowering, the branch polarity and the single virtual slot offset are all read directly from live disassembly and corroborated by two caller families and a structural sibling, but the owning class and the concrete callee at slot +0x70 are not established, and that is a material element under the batch definition. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY: a real behavioural claim is made and the whole computation is reconstructed. The bound is named: owning type and the +0x70 implementation.
semantic_findings: The override field at +0x18 and this function are mutually recursive in role: the constructor at 0x00b47730 calls this function and writes the result back into +0x18, so the field is a memoisation of this computation rather than an independent input.

The selector at +0x04 has exactly three distinguished values, 0, 1 and 2, proved by the three SUB/JZ pairs; values 0 and 1 are indistinguishable in this body, which suggests the distinction lives in a sibling's handling.

The sibling 0x00b3d9c0 reads the same selector and the same sub-object but calls slot +0x6c and returns a midpoint, so the sub-object exposes two adjacent services: a scalar magnitude at +0x70 and a 6-float point pair at +0x6c.

The constructor initialises +0x10 and +0x14 to 1.0f and +0x18 to 0.0f, so a freshly constructed object with selector 0 or 1 returns its sub-object's magnitude unchanged, and one with any other selector returns exactly +0.0f.
Because the early return precedes any selector work, an object whose +0x18 has been populated never touches the sub-object, which is the reason the constructor caches it.
There is no null check on receiver+0x40 anywhere in the body, so both the selector-2 arm and the selector-0/1 arm fault on a null sub-object; this is preserved, not defended against.
The function has zero direct callees other than the single virtual call and zero global reads, which is why the ledger recorded a 0-callee count.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this function? The address has 10 references, all UNCONDITIONAL_CALL, and no DATA reference, so it is not a vtable slot and no owner can be named.
What is the concrete callee at vtable slot +0x70 of the sub-object, and which vtable is it? No instance of the sub-object was ever observed at a callsite, so no table address could be read.

What is the sub-object at receiver+0x40? Only two virtual slots (+0x6c, +0x70) and a cached 3-float point at +0x40 are observed. The +0x6c slot writes a 6-float block that 0x00b3d9c0 averages pairwise and halves, which is consistent with a bounding pair of 3D points, but that is an inference and is not claimed as identity.
What do selector values 0 and 1 mean, and why are they the same here? The distinction must live in 0x00b3d9c0 or elsewhere; the enum has no name.
What is the separate enum at receiver+0x0c, compared against 2 at 0x00b42630 and against 0 at 0x00b4780b? It is not the selector this body switches on.
Is the FLT_MAX comparison in the constructor a saturating guard or a validity flag? The two instructions observed do not distinguish those readings.
Is the +0x14 float, initialised to 1.0f next to the +0x10 multiplier, a second factor this function does not use? No read of +0x14 was found in this body.
No original-process trace exists, so none of the above can be closed statically and the runtime values of the sub-object are unverified.
